Resolve #2514


Test `Preview works for files` has been modified to also include the case where the preview did not start from zero cursor position. As a consequence, I had to regenerate some screenshots in test cases also using the `real_path` directory.

comment_data.body:
I understand that this reproduces the issue, but it still isn't quite clear as to what is the *true* culprit is here. Like, if this is only reproducible with \*.h file, then there has to be some option or combinations of them that produces this result.

Locating the problem to this level will probably allow to reuse existing files (in a separate test) by first setting these options once or in the `FileType` autocommand.

I think I like the [idea of passing `view` directly](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2514#issuecomment-5006218653) more. Renaming the function to `H.window_set_view_cursor()` and not using early return (i.e. `if view.was_focused then H.window_tweak_cursor(...) end`) looks like the cleanest approach here.

comment_data.body:
```suggestion
  local is_dir = H.fs_get_type(buf_data.path) == 'directory'
  if type(view.cursor) == 'table' then
    pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, win_id, view.cursor)
    -- Tweak cursor here and don't rely on `CursorMoved` event to reduce flicker
    if is_dir then pcall(H.window_tweak_cursor, win_id, buf_id) end
  end
```

This approach allows reusing the single check (please also use it when setting `'cursorline'`) of the path type and buffer identifier.

comment_regular_data.body:
Oh, I only now have seen the second edit of [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/issues/2514#issuecomment-5006218653). The culprit is that the file contains a line with three or more `/` which are recognized as special indicators in directory buffers. This information is definitely needed in the commit message at least.

If that's the case, then I the more appropriate solution is to not tweak cursor when window shows a buffer for a file. And instead of adding a new file, prepending the `a.txt` test file with the wide line that contains three slashes with a text explanation in between is a less intrusive and more direct way to test this.

I think inlining the `H.window_set_cursor()` directly into the only place it is used is more beneficial here, since it can reuse the `H.fs_get_type(buf_data.path)` data to determine if the cursor needs to be tweaked.

I pushed a new commit. 

For the test I used `b.txt`...
